_about: This is the complete persistent, non-secret VANTARI configuration surface. Keys beginning with an underscore are documentation metadata and do not change runtime behavior.
VANTARI_HOME is intentionally not configurable here because it locates this file. Set it in the launching process when the default ~/.vantari directory must change.

Provider credentials, base URL, account metadata, and the active provider belong in the sibling auth.json file. Agent routes may reference a provider id and override its model, but never carry credentials.
Host and port, per-turn context/output overrides, tool timeouts, and output caps are invocation-scoped controls; they remain CLI, RPC, or tool arguments rather than persistent global policy.
Precedence is invocation argument, process environment, config.json environment entry, typed config section, then the compiled default where that layer applies.

_help.version: Configuration schema version. Version 1 is the only supported value; change it only when migrating to a schema explicitly supported by the installed binary.

_help.workspace: Optional persistent workspace path used when no VANTARI_WORKSPACE process or environment entry is set and no workspace is discovered from the current directory. Null keeps automatic discovery.
_help.max_steps: Maximum agent execution steps allowed in one run. Raise deliberately for long autonomous work; lower it to bound cost and runaway loops.
_help.max_tool_calls_per_turn: Maximum tool calls accepted from a single provider turn. This limits oversized or cyclic tool batches before effects execute.
_help.max_tool_calls_per_session: Maximum cumulative tool calls across one session. It is the session-wide safety budget and must be at least as large as the per-turn limit.
_help.full_access_mode: When false (default), agent file and process paths stay inside the active workspace. Set true only when the operator explicitly wants agents to work in other directories.
_help.log_level: Chat detail posture: silent (default) hides internal telemetry and repetition, normal shows concise operational checkpoints, and full permits diagnostic lifecycle detail. Durable event and session ledgers remain complete at every level.
_help.effort: Provider effort/reasoning level: low, medium, high, or max. Controls reasoning depth on models that accept the effort parameter. Null uses the provider default.
_help.temperature: Provider sampling temperature (0.0-2.0). Lower is more deterministic. Null uses the provider default; the compiled default sends 0 for determinism.

_help.theme: Named renderer palette: vantari (default), midnight, high_contrast, or amber. The palette changes the existing TUI surfaces without adding per-cell color configuration.
_help.status_bar_position: Place the compact status/context row at the bottom (default) or top of the chat viewport. The composer remains at the bottom.

_help.wire_api: Provider HTTP protocol shape. auto (default) detects from the base URL: api.anthropic.com resolves to anthropic_messages; every other OpenAI-compatible endpoint (z.ai, deepseek, openai, LM Studio, Ollama) resolves to chat_completions. Explicit values (chat_completions, responses, anthropic_messages) always override detection. This does not select credentials or a model.

_help.max_concurrency: Maximum in-process agent or model-task workers allowed to execute concurrently. Additional admitted tasks remain queued in the same parent-owned supervisor. A changed value replaces the one physical pool at the next idle capacity boundary; active work drains under the actual prior ceiling.
_help.roles: Optional operator-owned overrides keyed by general, recon, planning, compaction, implementation, review, or validation. Each role accepts provider_id, model, wire_api, thinking_mode, effort, temperature, context_window_tokens, and reserve_output_tokens. A provider_id references auth.json; credentials, execution kind, and capability profile never appear here.
_help.prompt_modes: Optional model/provider overrides keyed by orchestrate, build, align, or plan. They reuse the same unified route identity and apply only to the next root turn; omitted fields inherit the active route.

_help.orchestrator_only: When true, a root session receives only agent-control tools, must call agents before dispatch, and delegates artifact-heavy work into isolated child context windows. Child capability profiles are unchanged.
_help.definitions: Editable fixed specialist personas. Built-in ids may override the fields shown here. A new lowercase snake_case id must set extends to one built-in id; inheritance fixes execution kind and capability profile while the definition may tune persona, condition, route role, budgets, output contract, doctrine tags, ticket ownership, checkpoint contract, autonomy, effort, and temperature. effort/temperature null or absent = VANTARI (the kernel) decides. Changes hot-load on the next agents snapshot.

general.description: Bounded general-purpose VAR1 child session with ticket discipline.
general.when_to_use: Use when no narrower specialist owns the task, or when the ticket needs a flexible executor with delegation latitude.
general.instruction: TICKET DISCIPLINE: own your assigned ticket; drive it to complete; mark complete only when proven; NEVER close (kernel-only). KEEP the checkpoint summary current (>=3 sentences: status, evidence, next action) so the parent and siblings read your state live. Return a concise SITREP: findings, evidence paths, uncertainty, blockers, residual risk. Evidence-first: every claim carries file:line or command receipt.

recon.description: Read-only repository or evidence reconnaissance. IX search, exact provenance.
recon.when_to_use: Use when ownership, architecture, dependencies, or exact source evidence must be mapped before any decision or mutation.
recon.instruction: INSPECT ONLY. Evidence-first: cite exact paths, file:line, and commands; record uncertainty and residual risk; never guess - source or retract. Use IX search contracts; never substitute ad hoc readers. Findings-ledger shape: defect/owner/evidence/acceptance. Keep the checkpoint summary current.

planner.description: One-turn plan synthesis from supplied evidence. Planning-spec protocol distillation.
planner.when_to_use: Use after reconnaissance when supplied evidence must become an ordered, gated implementation contract.
planner.instruction: USE ONLY SUPPLIED CONTEXT. Return an ordered plan: decomposed phases, dependency edges, invariants preserved, proof gates per phase, blocker protocol, stop conditions. Every phase maps to source evidence; no invented owners. State the falsification hook that catches a shallow execution.

spec.description: One-turn spec/contract author. System boundary, owners, dependency order, ratchet targets.
spec.when_to_use: Use when a feature or chain needs an authoritative parent spec: boundary, canonical owners, sequencing, improvement ratchet, research agenda.
spec.instruction: AUTHOR THE CONTRACT, not prose. Name the system boundary, canonical owners, dependency and risk ordering, chain-level improvement ratchet (better-than-before deltas), and bounded research agenda with evidence surfaces. Source-message anchors verbatim; every slice carries a proof obligation. Reject skeletal specs.

compactor.description: One-turn dense summary wording over supplied artifacts. Entry-aware compression.
compactor.when_to_use: Use when supplied evidence must be compressed without losing decisions, owners, or unresolved state.
compactor.instruction: PRESERVE decisions, evidence, active state, unresolved risks, and exact owner paths; compacted ranges stay source-truth under the full transcript. Do not invent facts. Bounded aggressiveness: higher compaction may re-summarize; never drop a decision or owner.

implementer.description: Bounded implementation branch with read, write, and command capability. Ticket owner.
implementer.when_to_use: Use when one isolated file or module slice can be implemented and validated independently as its own ticket.
implementer.instruction: TICKET OWNER: own the assigned ticket, drive it to complete, mark complete ONLY when proven (tests + evidence), NEVER close (kernel-only). Own only the assigned files; preserve concurrent work. Write-capable tools emit effect evidence: resolved path, byte counts, hashes. Keep the checkpoint summary current; return a diff-grounded SITREP with validation receipts.

doc_writer.description: High-step document writer for large file persistence with verification.
doc_writer.when_to_use: Use when a large file (docs, ledgers, generated artifacts) must be written and verified in bounded slices.
doc_writer.instruction: PERSIST IN SLICES: write, verify byte counts and structure, then continue; never leave a torn tail. Docs describe shipped runtime truth, not intended future state. Keep the checkpoint summary current; return a SITREP with written paths, byte counts, and verification receipts.

scaffold.description: Chain scaffold: decomposes work into planning-spec chains / findings-ledgers with proof gates.
scaffold.when_to_use: Use when work requires decomposed execution chains, state-machine handoff, invariant preservation, or crash recovery.
scaffold.instruction: SCAFFOLD THE CHAIN: source-message anchors verbatim -> category purity -> repository ownership recon -> parent + lettered units -> dependency edges -> quality gates (test floor, idempotency contract, blast radius, rollback) -> evidence-gated single-move archival -> terminal QC review. Every unit carries entry state, exit state, handoff contract. Skeletal slices are failures.

orchestrator_parent.description: Parent orchestrator: aggressive fan-out delegation, live monitoring, ticket assignment and closure review.
orchestrator_parent.when_to_use: Use when orchestrating multi-agent work with constant parallel delegation, ticket assignment, and completion review.
orchestrator_parent.instruction: DELEGATION DISCIPLINE - AGGRESSIVE: fan out ALL branchable work immediately; never one agent when two can run parallel; background:true always; poll agent_status non-blocking; never sit idle - launch the next independent stream while agents fly. TICKET AUTHORITY: assign tickets to specialists; each agent owns its ticket state; agents mark complete but ONLY YOU close or reopen/reassign, ALWAYS with written reasoning; a reopened ticket is re-assigned immediately to a fresh specialist. Read child checkpoint summaries to synthesize; reconcile contradictions; publish ONE parent-owned conclusion. Live status table after every action.
orchestrator_parent.doctrine_tags: ticket-discipline parallel-fanout live-monitor reconcile-contradictions parent-owned-conclusion close-with-reasoning

harvester.description: Competitive intelligence harvester: nsect/insect research, source-proof benchmarks.
harvester.when_to_use: Use when competitor research, market analysis, feature benchmarking, or evidence harvesting must precede a decision.
harvester.instruction: RESEARCH HARVEST DOCTRINE - THREE LAWS: (1) NEVER GUESS: source every claim to URL or file:line; (2) HARVEST WIDE: 3-5+ queries per competitor, then benchmark deep against our source; (3) PROVE OR RETRACT. Competitor mistakes are free education, successes are stolen blueprints. Six-competitor floor for decisions; twelve for deep mechanisms. Write findings to the evidence ledger with provenance.

reviewer.description: One-turn supplied-artifact review. QC 4/4 maintainer judgment.
reviewer.when_to_use: Use when a bounded artifact set needs an independent findings-first review without tool access.
reviewer.instruction: QC 4/4 JUDGMENT: structure (maintainer-grade ownership, no parallel systems), contract truth (capability proven through the real consumer path), test pressure (falsification, not ceremony), code quality (anti-pattern sweep: hidden fallbacks, drift, fake simplicity). Severity-ordered findings with exact referents and falsification notes.

validator.description: Read-only validation branch for independent falsification proof.
validator.when_to_use: Use when commands or source checks can independently falsify an implementation claim without mutation.
validator.instruction: FALSIFY, DO NOT CONFIRM: run bounded validation probes without mutation; treat a passing test as valuable only when it proves an invariant a shallow implementation would violate. Return commands, observed outputs, failures, and residual risk. Adversarial pipeline probes: poisoned suffixes, stale owners, torn writes, same-millisecond bursts.

_help.auto_compaction: Allows the context compiler to create checkpoints automatically near the configured token threshold. The append-only transcript remains intact.
_help.manual_compaction: Allows explicit operator-triggered session compaction. Disable only when checkpoint writes must be prohibited entirely.
_help.context_window_tokens: Provider context capacity in tokens. Null enables provider/model detection with the compiled default as fallback; a positive integer pins the capacity.
_help.compact_at_ratio_milli: Automatic compaction threshold in thousandths of usable context capacity. 850 means 85 percent; valid values are 1 through 1000.
_help.reserve_output_tokens: Tokens held back from input context for the next model output. It also becomes the default maximum output budget unless a turn supplies an explicit override.
_help.keep_recent_messages: Minimum number of newest transcript messages retained verbatim after a compacted checkpoint so current conversational state remains precise.
_help.max_entries_per_checkpoint: Maximum transcript entries summarized into one checkpoint. Zero means no entry-count cap; token and lifecycle boundaries still apply.
_help.aggressiveness_milli: Compaction strength in thousandths. Higher values produce denser summaries; valid values are 0 through 1000.
_help.retry_on_provider_overflow: When true, a provider context-overflow response may trigger one compiler rebuild and retry through the canonical checkpoint path.

_help.system_prompt_file: Optional workspace-relative path to an additional non-empty system prompt file. Null uses only the kernel-owned system prompt.
_help.developer_prompt_file: Optional workspace-relative path to an additional non-empty developer prompt file. Null supplies no operator-managed developer prompt.
_help.persona: Optional inline persona description injected after the system prompt identity. Controls tone, voice, technical level, and communication style. Null omits the layer.
_help.guardrails: Optional inline user-owned guardrails injected after internal runtime guardrails. Use for prompt-injection protection, safety boundaries, or domain-specific constraints. Null omits the layer; the kernel-owned internal guardrails always apply.
_help.user_context: Optional inline custom context bolted on after the developer prompt. Use for project-specific instructions, operator preferences, or extra context the agent should always carry. Null omits the layer.

prompts.persona: Senior systems engineer. Direct, technical, no hedging. Forbidden openings: 'I'll go ahead and', 'Let me', 'Based on my analysis'. State findings, then evidence, then next action. Distinguish known (verified) from suspected (inferred) from guessing (speculative) — label each. Military-focused checkpoints: 'Scanning dependency graph for injection points' not 'I am currently analyzing the dependency structure of the project to find potential dependency injection locations.' Every word costs a token and an attention unit; spend both like they're finite.

_help.enabled: When true, a lightweight draft model restructures the user's input into a compiled prompt before the heavyweight model starts. Reduces ambiguity and improves first-token latency. The draft model runs synchronously on submit.
_help.model: The model id for the draft layer. Should be a fast/lightweight model. Defaults to glm-5-turbo.
_help.provider_id: Optional provider id from auth.json for the draft model. Null uses the active provider.
_help.effort: Effort level for the draft model: low, medium, high, max. Low is recommended for speed.
_help.temperature: Sampling temperature for the draft model. Lower is more deterministic.

_help.enabled: When true, a lightweight buffer model runs concurrently with the heavyweight model, producing navigation previews (next steps, directions, insights). The preview is shown in the TUI reasoning dock when the heavyweight is idle, and injected as context into the next turn.
_help.model: The model id for the buffer layer. Should be a fast/lightweight model. Defaults to glm-5-turbo.
_help.provider_id: Optional provider id from auth.json for the buffer model. Null uses the active provider.
_help.effort: Effort level for the buffer model: low, medium, high, max.
_help.temperature: Sampling temperature for the buffer model. Slightly higher for diverse predictions.
_help.interval_ms: Minimum milliseconds between buffer model invocations. Prevents excessive calls during fast turn cycles.

_help.enabled: Loads bounded active session and global memories into the agent prompt. False preserves the files and tools but disables automatic recall.
_help.agent_writes_enabled: Allows memory_write calls initiated by the agent or an explicit user request. False makes memory read-only to agent runs.
_help.max_entry_bytes: Maximum UTF-8 bytes in one topic plus content payload. This prevents memory from becoming a transcript or document store.
_help.max_session_context_bytes: Maximum bytes of active session-only memory compiled into one provider prompt rebuild.
_help.max_global_context_bytes: Maximum bytes of active cross-workspace memory compiled into one provider prompt rebuild.
_help.max_context_entries: Maximum combined active memory entries compiled into one provider prompt rebuild. Session entries are considered before global entries.

_help.VANTARI_WORKSPACE: File-backed equivalent of the VANTARI_WORKSPACE process variable. A real process variable with the same name wins; null leaves this layer unset.
_help.MAX_STEPS: File-backed environment-style override for runtime.max_steps. Accepts a positive integer or decimal string; the real MAX_STEPS process variable wins.
_help.MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_TURN: File-backed environment-style override for runtime.max_tool_calls_per_turn. Accepts a positive integer or decimal string; the real process variable wins.
_help.MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_SESSION: File-backed environment-style override for runtime.max_tool_calls_per_session. Accepts an integer or decimal string at least as large as the effective per-turn limit; the real process variable wins.
